## What to do, and how long it takes

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | Read Kowalski & Legendre (2023) | 45 min |
| **2** | Read Le Billon & Shykora (2020) | 30 min |
| **3** | Collect three datasets; **transcribe four USGS tables** | 40 min |
| **4** | Attempt the self-check | 15 min |

::: {.warn}
The practice round starts from your transcription. No transcription, no practice.
:::

## 1 · The big work

**Kowalski & Legendre (2023), *Raw Materials Critical for the Green Transition*, OECD Trade Policy Papers 269**

::: {.muted}
[doi:10.1787/c6bb598b-en](https://doi.org/10.1787/c6bb598b-en) · free
:::

| | |
|---|---|
| **1** | How is **concentration** measured? |
| **2** | How is the **restrictions inventory** built? |
| **3** | The **strongest evidence** that restrictions spread after 2009 |
| **4** | One **limitation** a procurement director would raise |

::: {.get}
**Targets:** restrictions over time · concentration of production by country.
:::

## 2 · The companion reading

**Le Billon & Shykora (2020), *Conflicts, commodities and the environmental geopolitics of supply chains***

::: {.muted}
In S. O'Lear (Ed.), *A Research Agenda for Environmental Geopolitics*, pp. 59–73 · [doi:10.4337/9781788971249.00012](https://doi.org/10.4337/9781788971249.00012)
:::

- What makes a commodity a **conflict** commodity?
- How do supply chains **carry** conflict and harm to consumers?
- One governance response — and why it falls short

::: {.step}
Revisit **Farrell & Newman (2019)**: *chokepoint* and *panopticon* — definitions only.
:::

## 3 · Collect — and transcribe

| Dataset | Where | What |
|---|---|---|
| **OECD export restrictions** | OECD Data Explorer | full table, CSV |
| **USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries** | usgs.gov | cobalt, graphite, lithium, rare earths — **transcribe** the world-production tables |
| **GSCPI** | newyorkfed.org | `gscpi_interactive_data.csv` — find the **latest vintage** |

::: {.warn}
Transcription rules: latest estimated year · drop *World total* · keep *Other countries* flagged · blanks for withheld values · write the unit.
:::

::: {.muted}
Split the minerals across the team. One person checks every row against the PDF.
:::

## 4 · Self-check

1. **Chokepoint** vs **panopticon**: one example of each
2. Shares 70%, 20%, 10%. **HHI?** Highly concentrated?
3. Two reasons to restrict ore exports **other than** coercion
4. A product of your team's firm that stops without one of the four minerals

## Arrive with

::: {.check}
- Both readings annotated; target figures located
- OECD CSV and GSCPI CSV in `data/raw/`
- `usgs_world_production.csv` complete and checked
- Provenance log started
- Self-check, on paper
:::
